If sentiment is predominantly bullish (≥0.67) in the last 5 days, reduce forecasted price by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to align with downward momentum.  
If sentiment is predominantly bearish (≤0.33) in the last 5 days, increase forecasted price by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract overconfidence.  
In mid-horizon (8–15 days), if sentiment swings from bullish to bearish, shift forecast downward by 2–3% for the next 3–5 days.  
In late-horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment remains bearish and forecast is still rising, apply a 3–5% downward correction to avoid overcorrection.  
If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast shows strong upward trend, reduce slope by 0.5–1.0% per day in mid-horizon to reflect sentiment uncertainty.  
If sentiment is consistently bullish but forecast is flat or declining, add 0.5–1.0% upward bias in late-horizon to capture sentiment-driven rebound potential.
